source: The shares of income people name when they talk about giving. The 2% row is the long-run US average share of income given to charity, rounded (Giving USA reports it near 2% of disposable income year after year); the 10% row is the tithe. Conventions, not benchmarks.
confidenceNote: None of these is a financial rule. 2% is a rounded population average, not a target; the tithe is a religious convention. The deduction note is a statement of how the US federal deduction works, not a rate.
note: the shares of income people give, and what each is called

shares.note: the US average share of income given (rounded)
the tithe (a religious convention, not a financial one)

deduction.note: Gifts to qualifying charities are deductible only when itemising. Most filers take the standard deduction, so a gift usually costs its face value. Not modelled here.
